findings: The company reports utilizing an automatic consistency control refrigeration system that monitors motor firmness values up to a threshold of "99" to regulate the cooling and freeze cylinder cycle, as detailed in the Donper D500 and D150 equipment manuals.

The company reports using a built-in air pump system across its "A" series models, such as the D828A, D840A, and D860A, which injects air into the mix during freezing to maintain consistent overrun control.

The company reports incorporating a patented utility model system for soft ice cream machines featuring an on-line rotational speed detection type control, where a central processing unit and revolution speed transducer track output shafts to control the consistency and softness of the product.

The company reports integrating an electric temperature control system with a temperature sensor attached to the outer wall of the ice cream machine's freezing cylinder to automatically adjust and stabilize temperature thresholds.
The company reports that its D880A twin-twist floor model soft-serve machine incorporates a high overrun air pump and an RPM control system to regulate texture and consistency.

We verified that the company's capabilities rest on its proprietary electronic monitoring components, including a patented on-line rotational speed system and integrated wall sensors for temperature-based freezing cylinder regulation, alongside factory-configured air pumps for overrun injection.
